summary: Implemented WorkspaceOrchestrator class in src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts with createWorkspace(), deleteWorkspace(), and renameWorkspace() methods.

createWorkspace() creates the workspace folder, clones all project repositories in parallel (using cloneRepository()), and generates a VS Code .code-workspace file. Partial failures are captured per-repository and do not abort workspace creation.

deleteWorkspace() enforces STABLE protection, validates the resolved workspace path is under projectsFolder via path.resolve+startsWith guard, recursively removes the folder, removes the VS Code file, and removes the workspace data entry via WorkspaceManager.remove().

renameWorkspace() enforces STABLE protection, pre-validates workspace existence before any filesystem changes, renames the folder with fs.renameSync, generates the new VS Code workspace file with updated folder paths, removes the old VS Code file, and updates the data entry via WorkspaceManager.rename().
Added comprehensive test suite in src/tests/workspace-orchestrator.test.ts with 18 tests covering all 7 acceptance criteria.
Full test suite: 293 tests, 0 failures.

comments.note: workspace-orchestrator.ts: createWorkspace() does not create the workspace data entry — callers must call WorkspaceManager.create() separately before createWorkspace(). This asymmetry (createWorkspace does not create data; deleteWorkspace does delete data) is minor but could lead to confusion. A follow-up could unify creation flow so the orchestrator owns the full lifecycle.

workspace-orchestrator.ts: renameWorkspace() reads project data via projectManager.getById() to check workspace existence, rather than delegating to workspaceManager.getById(). This is an intentional early-exit to avoid partial filesystem changes on stale-data failure. The pattern is slightly inconsistent with how workspaceManager.rename() later re-validates, but is safe and correct.

vscode-workspace.ts: generateWorkspaceFile() accepts repoPaths as { slug: string; path: string }[]. The slug property is never used inside the function body — only path is referenced. This could be simplified to { path: string }[] to remove the dead parameter field. No functional impact.

summary: Reviewed 4 files: src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts, src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts, src/git/git-clone.ts, src/git/git-cli.ts. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (path-traversal guard asymmetry in renameWorkspace — defense-in-depth only, not currently exploitable), 2 Low. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: MEDIUM — A01 (Broken Access Control / Path Traversal — Defense-in-Depth Gap): src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts — renameWorkspace() has no path-traversal guard, unlike deleteWorkspace() which correctly validates path.resolve(wsFolder).startsWith(resolvedProjectsFolder + path.sep) before any filesystem I/O. In renameWorkspace(), oldWsFolder and newWsFolder are computed from projectId and workspaceId without equivalent resolution checks. Current upstream validation (projectId constrained to kebab-case /^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/, workspaceId constrained to /^[A-Z]{2,6}$/) makes exploitation impossible through normal code paths — neither format can encode path separators or dot-segments. However, the asymmetry means any future relaxation of ID validation rules would silently introduce a path traversal vector. Recommendation: Add the same guard used in deleteWorkspace() to renameWorkspace() immediately after the STABLE check and project existence check and before any fs.renameSync/generateWorkspaceFile calls: const resolvedOld = path.resolve(oldWsFolder); const resolvedProjectsFolder = path.resolve(this.config.projectsFolder); if (!resolvedOld.startsWith(resolvedProjectsFolder + path.sep)) { throw new Error(...); }

LOW — A04 (Insecure Design / Atomicity): src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts renameWorkspace() — newId format and uniqueness validation is performed inside workspaceManager.rename() (line ~240), which is called AFTER fs.renameSync(), generateWorkspaceFile(), and removeWorkspaceFile(). If workspaceManager.rename() throws (e.g. invalid newId format or collision), the filesystem has already been mutated (folder renamed to newId, old .code-workspace file deleted, new one written) while the data entry remains unchanged. The system is left in an inconsistent state. Not a direct security vulnerability given the [A-Z]{2,6} constraint, but it could lead to orphaned filesystem artefacts. Recommendation: Pre-validate newId with isValidWorkspaceId(newId) at the top of renameWorkspace() before any filesystem operations, so invalid IDs are rejected before any I/O.

LOW — A02 (Cryptographic Failures / Cleartext Transport): src/git/git-clone.ts ALLOWED_URL_PREFIXES includes 'http://'. Cloning over plain HTTP exposes repository contents and any embedded credentials (e.g. http://user:token@host/repo) to network interception. While practical for intranet or local use, it's an unencrypted channel boundary. Recommendation: Document the cleartext-transport risk in the AppConfig or README so operators can make an informed decision; optionally add a config flag to disable http:// if the tool is ever used in a CI/CD or shared-network context.

INFO — A09 (Security Logging): src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts — deleteWorkspace() and renameWorkspace() perform destructive/irreversible filesystem operations but produce no audit trail. For a developer tool this is acceptable today, but if the tool evolves to a multi-user or daemon mode, the absence of structured logging for workspace delete/rename events would make incident investigation difficult. No immediate action required.

summary: [FAIL] Two blocking defects found.

(1) src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts generateWorkspaceFile(): assigns an identical name to every folder entry — the `slug` parameter is passed by all callers but never used in name construction, producing indistinguishable roots in VS Code Explorer for multi-repo projects.

(2) src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts renameWorkspace(): atomicity bug when oldId === newId — the new .code-workspace file is written and immediately deleted (same resolved path), leaving the workspace with a valid data entry but a missing file; workspaceManager.rename() throws only after the damage is done.
Both defects are undetected by the test suite (tests use single-repo projects; no same-ID rename test exists).
Code structure and documentation quality are excellent: JSDoc is thorough, STABLE protection is consistently enforced, and the private-helper decomposition is clean.
Security Auditor-flagged path-traversal guard asymmetry and pre-validation ordering should be addressed in the same Developer pass.

comments.note: BLOCKING — src/orchestration/vscode-workspace.ts generateWorkspaceFile(): All folder entries in the .code-workspace file receive the same `name` value (`${projectName} (${workspaceId})`). The `repoPaths` parameter carries a `slug` field (the repository ID) that is never referenced inside the function. For a project with N repositories, every entry in the VS Code `folders` array shares an identical label, making them indistinguishable in VS Code Explorer — a critical UX failure for a multi-repo workspace tool. Fix: use `repo.slug` as the distinguishing component in the folder name, e.g. name: `${repo.slug} (${workspaceId})` or name: repo.slug. The shared `folderName` constant can be removed. NOTE: The Developer observation (#3 in implementation pipeline) misidentified this as 'simplify to { path: string }[]'; the correct fix is to USE the slug in the name. Tests must also be updated: the rename content test asserts `parsed.folders[0].path` but never checks `.name`.

BLOCKING — src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts renameWorkspace(): calling renameWorkspace(projectId, 'DEV', 'DEV') (oldId === newId) leaves the workspace in a broken state. Execution path: (1) fs.renameSync(same, same) — no-op; (2) generateWorkspaceFile writes to newFilePath which equals oldFilePath; (3) removeWorkspaceFile(oldFilePath) deletes the file just written; (4) workspaceManager.rename() throws 'workspace DEV already exists'. End state: data entry intact, .code-workspace file deleted — permanently broken with no recovery path. Fix: add pre-I/O validation at the top of renameWorkspace() after the STABLE check and after loading `project`: (a) if (!isValidWorkspaceId(newId)) throw — rejects before any I/O; (b) if (newId === oldId) throw 'Cannot rename: newId must differ from oldId'; (c) if (newId in project.Workspaces) throw — pre-checks uniqueness using already-loaded project data. This ensures all data-layer rejections happen before fs.renameSync.

PATH-TRAVERSAL GUARD ASYMMETRY (Security Auditor Medium, carried forward): renameWorkspace() should add the same guard as deleteWorkspace(). After the pre-I/O validation additions, insert: const resolvedOld = path.resolve(oldWsFolder); const resolvedProjectsFolder = path.resolve(this.config.projectsFolder); if (!resolvedOld.startsWith(resolvedProjectsFolder + path.sep)) { throw new Error(`Security check failed: workspace path ${resolvedOld} is not under projectsFolder ${resolvedProjectsFolder}.`); }. Non-behavioral for all currently valid inputs — closes the defense-in-depth asymmetry.

TEST COVERAGE GAPS: (1) renameWorkspace(projectId, 'DEV', 'DEV') — the same-ID atomicity bug is completely undetected; (2) renameWorkspace with invalid newId format (e.g. 'AB1') — should confirm the workspace file is NOT mutated; (3) multi-repo createWorkspace test validating that each folder entry in the .code-workspace file has a distinct `name`. All three should be added alongside the blocking defect fixes.
